title: Ambient categories and small subcategories
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and choose $\tau=\mathrm{\acute et}$ or $\mathrm{pro\acute et}$, with small site $T_\tau$ as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] or [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], using the universes and small skeleton of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a sheaf of commutative rings $R_T$ on that site, let $\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ be the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its ambient categories are
$$
D(T_\tau,R_T):=D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)),\qquad
D^+(T_\tau,R_T),\quad D^-(T_\tau,R_T),\quad D^b(T_\tau,R_T),
$$
where $D$ is the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the three full subcategories are defined by cohomology vanishing in sufficiently negative degrees, sufficiently positive degrees, and outside a finite interval, respectively [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. For a commutative ring $R$, the notation $D(T_\tau,R)$ uses the constant sheaf $R_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; on the etale site this is [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

For a set of primes $P$ invertible on $T$, define $D^+_{P\text{-tor}}(T_\tau,R_T)$ to be the full subcategory [def-sf-induced-category] of $D^+(T_\tau,R_T)$ on the objects $K$ such that, for every integer $i$, every geometric point $\bar t$ and every element $x$ of the underlying abelian group of $\mathcal H^i(K)_{\bar t}$, there is an integer $m>0$ with $mx=0$ and all prime divisors of $m$ in $P$. Here $\mathcal H^i$ is the cohomology sheaf [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and the stalk is [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] for $\tau=\mathrm{\acute et}$ and [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] for $\tau=\mathrm{pro\acute et}$. This extends the abelian-etale notation of [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion] by applying its elementwise condition to the underlying cohomology stalk groups.

For the coefficient stages, fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ inside it with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$; put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Suppose $\ell$ is invertible on $T$ when using the finite-Tor conventions. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, define the small categories
$$
D^b_c(T_\tau,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b(T_\tau,\Lambda),\qquad
D^b_{ctf}(T_\tau,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b_c(T_\tau,\Lambda),\qquad
D_c^{[a,b]}(T_\tau,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b_c(T_\tau,\Lambda)
$$
for integers $a\le b$ as follows. The first consists of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology, using [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] on the etale site and [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] on the pro-etale site. The second consists of those objects having finite Tor amplitude: for some integers $u\le v$, tensoring with every degree-zero $\Lambda_T$-module sheaf gives cohomology only in $[u,v]$, using [def-kun-tor-amplitude] on the etale site and [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on the pro-etale site. The third consists of the objects $K$ with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-constructible-intervals, def-weil-derived-category-cohomological-support]. All these are full subcategories: morphisms, identities and composition are inherited from the containing category [def-sf-induced-category].

At the integral stage the ambient notation $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ instead uses the completed ring sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=\varprojlim_j(A_{E,j})_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The small category $D^b_c(T,\mathcal O_E)$ is the derived-complete category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], including its single cohomological interval bounding all reductions. Its full subcategory $D^b_{ctf}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ imposes one Tor interval for all reductions, as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. At the field stages use
$$
D^b_c(T,E):=D^b_c(T,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E],\qquad
D^b_c(T,\Qlb):=\mathop{\operatorname{2-colim}}_{E'\subset\Qlb,\ [E':\Ql]<\infty}D^b_c(T,E'),
$$
with exactly the scalar-localization and common-stage constructions of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Define $D^b_{ctf}(T,E):=D^b_c(T,E)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(T,\Qlb):=D^b_c(T,\Qlb)$ as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$, define $D_c^{[a,b]}(T,\Lambda)$ as the full subcategory on $D_c^{\ge a}(T,\Lambda)\cap D_c^{\le b}(T,\Lambda)$, using the standard pairs and their shifts from [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure]. These higher coefficient-stage categories have these pro-etale, localization and common-stage meanings; no identification with constant-coefficient etale categories, or embedding of the localized/common-stage categories in an ordinary constant-coefficient derived category, is part of this definition.
